message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals that belong to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Their most recent common ancestor was a small, early mammal that lived in the Paleocene–Eocene (roughly 70–60 million years ago). This ancestor was a member of the Laurasiatherian lineage that later split into the separate orders Carnivora (which gave rise to lions) and Perissodactyla (which gave rise to zebras).
